ai.summary: AMD reported a $1.07 billion non-cash charge tied to warrants granted under chip-supply agreements with OpenAI and Meta. The deals illustrate how AI companies and chipmakers are increasingly using equity incentives to secure large, long-term purchases.
ai.title: AMD's OpenAI, Meta chip deals trigger $1 billion quarterly charge

ai.summary: AMD reported record third-quarter revenue of $13.4 billion, with data-center sales reaching $8.5 billion. The company forecast about $17 billion in fourth-quarter revenue and said it expects revenue growth above 80% in 2027, driven chiefly by data centers.
ai.title: AMD rides data center riches to ‘largest and most profitable’ quarter in history

ai.summary: The outlet’s November 4 roundup reports that the New York Times and three academic publishers sued Brave over alleged AI-related content sales. The result is a notable escalation in disputes over the use and commercialization of publishers’ material by AI businesses.
ai.title: Brave Lawsuit: NYT and Three Papers Sue Over AI Content Sales

ai.summary: India’s MeitY announced three AI models under the IndiaAI Mission: EKA-1, designed for math, coding and reasoning, and two smaller Dhīr models intended to run on phones without an internet connection. The initiative aims to support local-language and offline use and reduce reliance on foreign AI systems.
ai.title: IndiaAI Mission's three indigenous AI models target offline mobile access, secure use in critical sectors

ai.summary: Anthropic announced FlashProve, a research prototype for cryptographically verifying that a specified model generated a response. The report says the system currently supports mixture-of-experts models and short outputs, so it is an early technical step rather than a general-purpose verification product.
ai.title: Anthropic Releases FlashProve Response Verification System

quantum.summary: IBM’s Quantum Nighthawk processor has been installed at Yonsei University, its first deployment at a customer institution’s own facility. The 120-programmable-qubit system is reported to run more than 100,000 circuits per second—25 times the throughput of the previous processor—and will support research and education.
quantum.title: IBM installs latest quantum processor at Yonsei University, enabling 100,000 circuits per second

quantum.summary: NVIDIA researchers describe an AI-assisted method for mapping topological error-correction codes onto hardware, tested with an eight-qubit toric-code array on a superconducting device. The approach uses formal verification and compares ways of bounding unwanted interactions to help guide hardware design.
quantum.title: Agentic Pipelines for Mapping Topological Codes to Quantum Hardware

quantum.summary: Researchers at the University of Wisconsin–Madison introduced MBUndo, a compiler pass that automatically converts circuits to use measurement-based uncomputation. On 22 benchmarks, they report T-gate-count reductions above 36.5% compared with existing uncomputation synthesizers.
quantum.title: Researchers Show How To Automatically Uncompute Ancilla Qubits With Measurements

quantum.summary: A study estimates that quantum advantage for the examined spin SYK-dot-chain simulations could require dots with 15–21 or more qubits and two-qubit gate error rates around 10⁻⁶. The result highlights how demanding the hardware precision could be for this proposed application.
quantum.title: A Quantum Advantage May Need Two-qubit Gates With 10⁻⁶ Error Rates

quantum.summary: German startup Quint Computing announced €9.1 million in initial financing to develop superconducting quantum processors intended to reduce computational errors through hardware architecture. The company says the funding will support chip engineering, hiring and initial industrial applications; its stated goal of cutting error-correction requirements remains a target, not a demonstrated result.
quantum.title: VC funding deals: Syncere, Quint Computing, Tumbleweed

quantum.summary: A new library, eigenkit, provides a common interface for quantum algorithms across 12 simulators and hardware platforms, including IBM Heron and IQM Emerald. Its developers say tests show that the best processor can depend on the algorithm, underscoring the value of portability across systems.
quantum.title: A Single Library Now Links Quantum Algorithms To IBM And IQM Hardware
